messages.content: 你能給我從舊金山家裡到帕羅奧圖辦公室最快的路線，然後從帕羅奧圖到舊金山金門大橋的風景路線，最後從金門大橋回家最快的路線嗎？

function.name: get_directions
function.description: Retrieve directions from one location to another. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

start_location.description: The starting point of the journey.

end_location.description: The destination point of the journey.

route_type.description: Type of route to use (e.g., fastest, scenic). Default is fastest.

message.reasoning: The user wants directions from home in San Francisco to Palo Alto office fastest route, then from Palo Alto to Golden Gate Bridge scenic route, then from Golden Gate Bridge back home fastest route. We need to call get_directions function twice? Actually three segments: home->Palo Alto, Palo Alto->Golden Gate Bridge, Golden Gate Bridge->home. We can call get_directions for each segment. Provide start_location and end_location. For first and third, route_type default fastest. For second, route_type scenic. We need to call function for each segment. Probably we should call get_directions three times. The function returns any. We'll call it with start_location: "San Francisco, CA" or "home" but we need actual addresses? The user says "from my home in San Francisco". We don't have exact address. We can use "San Francisco, CA" as start. For Palo Alto office, we can use "Palo Alto, CA". For Golden Gate Bridge, we can use "Golden Gate Bridge, San Francisco, CA". Then back home: start "Golden Gate Bridge, San Francisco, CA" to "San Francisco, CA". We'll call function three times.
